name: Sega Dreamcast family
summary: Explore the Dreamcast hardware across its four regional models. Region changes the BIOS and pack-in peripherals, not the hardware capability. The production revision decides whether MIL-CD booting still works — the final revisions removed MIL-CD support.

specs.memory: 26.125 MB total: 16 MB SDRAM main RAM + 8 MB SDRAM VRAM + 2 MB SDRAM sound RAM + 128 KB GD-ROM buffer
specs.storage: None internal; VMU memory cards in the controller
specs.media: GD-ROM (~1 GB); CD-ROM/CD-R via MIL-CD on most units
specs.display: 320×240 to 800×608 (TV), up to 1600×1200 internal; AV cable, optional VGA box
specs.network: Built-in 56k modem; broadband adapter sold separately

homebrew.name: MIL-CD boot
homebrew.firmware: No firmware to update; works on units that retain MIL-CD support
homebrew.summary: The console can boot code from a standard CD-R using the MIL-CD format, without a modchip. Sega left this path open on most units, but removed MIL-CD support from the final production revisions toward the end of the console's life.

compatibility.note: Works on most units. Late production revisions removed MIL-CD support — the model code alone does not tell you which revision is inside.

requirements: A CD-R with MIL-CD-compatible content and a unit that retained MIL-CD support.
warnings: Check MIL-CD support before buying a homebrew unit. Late revisions do not support it.
CD-R quality matters — the GD-ROM laser is hard on marginal media.

homebrew.name: KallistiOS
homebrew.firmware: Requires a MIL-CD-bootable disc or a hacked console
homebrew.summary: The homebrew minimal operating system most Dreamcast software uses. It supports most of the hardware but is not a multitasking OS.

compatibility.note: Most Dreamcast homebrew games, emulators and tools are built on KallistiOS.

requirements: A MIL-CD-bootable disc or an already-hacked console.
warnings: Not a multitasking OS — it is superfluous for games.

homebrew.name: DreamShell
homebrew.firmware: No firmware update; boots from CD-R (MIL-CD) or a supported SD/IDE adapter
homebrew.summary: An operating system for the Dreamcast built on the KallistiOS kernel, with a modular XML/Lua interface, drivers for storage and network devices, and an ISO loader that emulates BIOS calls to run disc images.

compatibility.note: The project builds for CD-R and storage-adapter boot and states no model limit; a late revision without MIL-CD needs the adapter route.

requirements: A DreamShell build for your boot method: a CD-R image or a supported SD/IDE adapter.
warnings: CD-R booting depends on the unit retaining MIL-CD support; the storage-adapter route needs the matching hardware.

homebrew.name: LinuxDC / NetBSD/dreamcast
homebrew.firmware: Historical ports; requires a hacked console
homebrew.summary: Linux and NetBSD ports existed for the Dreamcast. They do not really support the console's fast graphics — treat them as historical research, not usable desktops.

compatibility.note: Historical ports; graphics performance is poor.

warnings: Not a usable Linux install; graphics-poor historical ports.

homebrew.name: dreamcast.wiki homebrew index
homebrew.firmware: Requires a MIL-CD-bootable disc or a hacked console
homebrew.summary: A collection of homebrew games, emulators, media players and image viewers written to a bootable CD-R.

compatibility.note: Homebrew CD-Rs are normally region-free; retail games are region-locked to the BIOS.

requirements: A MIL-CD-bootable disc or a hacked console.

communities.name: DreamPi
communities.description: Raspberry Pi software that bridges the Dreamcast's built-in dial-up modem to Ethernet or Wi-Fi through a compatible USB voice modem, bringing compatible games and browsers back online without a dial-up ISP. It runs on all Raspberry Pi models except the Pi 5.

officialSupport.summary: Sega discontinued the Dreamcast in early 2001 after financial constraints; no official support or updates since.
